title: Biomass power plant waste‐derived poultry litter incineration ash as a novel nutrient solution source for hydroponic cultivation: Effect of sulfuric acid leaching and ash fraction
content:
Abstract

Poultry litter incineration ash (PLIA) represents a potentially valuable secondary resource for multi-nutrient recovery. This study aimed to characterize the mineralogical and chemical properties of different ash fractions, evaluate their transformation through sulfuric acid leaching, and assess the agronomic performance of the resulting ash-derived nutrient solutions in hydroponic-grown lettuce. Boiler ash (BA), fly ash (FA), and wet ash (WA) were chemically characterized and subjected to sulfuric acid leaching to produce stock nutrient solutions. A greenhouse experiment was conducted using lettuce grown in cocopeat with reference solution, BA, FA, and WA-derived solutions. Ash fractions showed strongly alkaline pH (10.3–13.5) and high nutrient heterogeneity, with FA rich in K, BA and WA rich in P and Ca, and all fractions containing substantial Fe, Zn, Cu, and Mn. Acid leaching significantly altered mineralogy, as evidenced by X-ray diffraction (XRD), indicating dissolution of Ca-phosphate phases and formation of secondary sulfate minerals. In lettuce, the reference solution produced the highest fresh weight, while ash-derived solutions enhanced N and micronutrient concentrations. Sulfuric acid extraction effectively converted PLIA into multi-nutrient hydroponic solutions by transforming poorly soluble phosphate minerals into more plant-available forms. Ash-derived nutrient solutions improved nutrient uptake and chlorophyll content, highlighting their potential for hydroponic cultivation.
